transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because I’m having a hard time staying focused. Like, I’ll start a safety briefing or go over a plan review really trying to pay attention, and within a few minutes my mind is on three other job problems. Then I end up missing things I know I should’ve caught.
Did you have trouble paying attention when you were a child?

Yeah, I did. Even back in elementary school, teachers were telling my parents I couldn’t stay in my seat, and I’d talk out of turn. I’d lose homework a lot too. I remember rushing through directions before I really understood what I was supposed to do.
Do these focus problems also happen outside of work, like at home or in everyday tasks?

Yeah, it happens at home too. It’s not just work. I’ll tell my wife I’m going to handle something, and then I forget or don’t follow through unless she reminds me over and over. She’s pretty worn down by it.

And at work it’s gotten serious too — missed follow-ups and me not keeping site coordination organized have led to my employer formally raising concerns. So it’s affecting both places.
Do you tend to worry excessively about a lot of different things?
I don’t know that I’d call it excessive worry. I mean, I think about work problems and stuff at home, sure, but I haven’t really noticed myself worrying about lots of different things all the time.
As an adult, do you often feel restless or fidgety?

Yeah, pretty often. Like in meetings, when everyone else is just sitting through it, I’m usually the one standing up, going to get coffee, stepping outside to check something, or finding some reason to move around. I have a hard time just staying seated the whole time.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a persistent pattern of inattention and hyperactivity/restlessness beginning in childhood and continuing into adulthood across multiple settings (work and home), with clear functional impairment. Childhood history includes inability to stay seated, talking out of turn, losing homework, and rushing through directions. Current symptoms include difficulty sustaining attention, forgetfulness/failure to follow through, disorganization, and frequent restlessness in meetings. This presentation is most consistent with ADHD, predominantly inattentive type / disturbance of activity and attention. Anxiety-related worry was specifically not prominent, making a primary anxiety disorder less likely.
